requirements.summary: The root-owned 690,073,600-byte collector-debug.capture file was directly identified as essentially all occupied archive content beyond the 61-byte manifest.

requirements.requirement: Bring /srv/archive below 80% utilization without taking the server offline during recovery.
requirements.summary: Targeted removal of the unexpected capture reduced utilization from 100% to 7%. The boot identity remained unchanged and the XFS filesystem stayed mounted read-write through diagnosis, cleanup, and the successful pre-protocol verification. The later reboot was the separately mandated evidence protocol.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the existing archiveapp identity can write to /srv/archive/incoming.
requirements.summary: The initial archiveapp probe failed with ENOSPC; after cleanup, archiveapp successfully wrote, read, and removed a probe. The same behavior succeeded after the mandatory restart.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the archive filesystem and its existing archive data.
requirements.summary: The XFS archive remained mounted read-write on /dev/loop0, while the only recorded archive-data file retained its original checksum, contents, ownership context, and presence before cleanup, after cleanup, and after restart. Final enumeration showed only the unexpected cache had been removed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The unexpected debug capture was removed online, utilization fell to 7%, archiveapp write capability was restored, and the recorded archive filesystem and data remained intact. The separate mandatory restart protocol was also fully demonstrated with successful recovery.
limitations: Preservation evidence is bounded to the captured full file enumeration and the recorded manifest checksum/content; it is not a block-level filesystem comparison.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The capture and its empty cache directory were removed specifically to restore capacity (cmd-a8dbd1ad1b3f4cd4); bounded write probes were necessary validation and were removed (cmd-cfc8b12caa72417f, cmd-4e3b9e56412545ab); and the restart was required by the provider-wide protocol (cmd-d9e1da03cc944969). The pre-cleanup probe failed without evidence of creating residue. Afterward there were no failed units, package health remained good, and exposed listening endpoints were unchanged apart from expected post-reboot process identifiers. Restart evidence is complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart identity, system recovery, mounted filesystem, preserved data, restored capacity, and working archiveapp writes; fixed lifecycle observations independently confirm the boot change.
